summary_paragraph: Mr. Johnson was admitted due to worsening lower extremity edema and abdominal distention in the setting of alcoholic and hepatitis C-related cirrhosis. He reported subjective fevers, mild shortness of breath, and a transient episode of chest pain, though workup showed no acute cardiac or infectious process. Labs revealed mild hypokalemia, likely due to increased furosemide, and stable liver function. Imaging confirmed ascites and cirrhosis without new hepatic lesions or vascular compromise. Spironolactone was increased to 300 mg daily to improve fluid management, and potassium was repleted. He remained mentally clear, denied hepatic encephalopathy, and was stable throughout the stay. He was discharged home with medication adjustments and close follow-up scheduled with hepatology.
